question_text: Was pCloud Pass hacked in November 2026?
answer_text: Yes, by its own account. pCloud says a cyberattack targeted its pCloud Pass password manager and was promptly contained. It says a small number of users' email addresses were exposed and login attempts were made.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Were passwords stored in pCloud Pass stolen?
what_would_settle_it: pCloud saying whether the attackers reached or copied any encrypted vaults, and whether any login attempt succeeded. pCloud says stored passwords were not compromised because they are encrypted.

question_text: Is pCloud's cloud storage affected by the pCloud Pass attack?
answer_text: pCloud says no: it says the incident was limited to pCloud Pass and its cloud storage service was not affected. Nobody outside the company has checked this.
label: Reported

question_text: Did the attackers get past two-factor authentication on pCloud Pass?
label: Not established
what_would_settle_it: pCloud saying whether any login attempt succeeded and how the new-device alerts were triggered. Customers with two-factor authentication on say they got the alert, but some saw no new device in their account.

question_text: Was the pCloud Pass new-device email itself a phishing email?
answer_text: Reported as genuine. pCloud says its system automatically notified each exposed address. The alert's link went to a pCloud test address, which pCloud has not explained. pCloud says it never asks for a Master Password by email.
label: Reported

question_text: How did the attackers get into pCloud Pass?
what_would_settle_it: pCloud saying how the attackers got in and when. Its statement mentions AI speeding up the discovery of software flaws, but does not name a flaw or say AI was used.
